translations.text: Jesse fathered King David, and David fathered Solomon by Uriah’s wife.
Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.

So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to Christ fourteen generations.
He came and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”

He said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here. For it is written: ‘He will give his angels orders concerning you, and they will lift you up on their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.’”
Again the devil took him up onto a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
You have heard that it was said, “You must not commit adultery.”
So that your charitable giving may be done in secret, and your Father, who sees you in secret, will reward you.
So that you do not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees you in secret, will reward you.
The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
So do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
Ask, and you will be given; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
So if you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit.
And then I will declare to them, “I never knew you. Get away from me, you who practice lawlessness!”
And look, a man with leprosy approached him and bowed down before him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have their dens, and the birds of the sky have their nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
Another of the disciples said to him, “Lord, first allow me to go and bury my father.”
While he was saying these things to them, look, a ruler approached him and bowed down before him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
Jesus got up and followed him, along with his disciples.
He said, “Go away, for the little girl has not died but is sleeping.” But they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
But they went out and spread the news about him throughout that whole region.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.
When they had gone, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?”
Then Jesus began to rebuke the cities where most of his miracles had taken place, because they had not repented.
Yes, my Father, because this was pleasing in your sight.
Come to me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”

The [?] of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom. And look, here is someone greater than Solomon!
But he said to them, “An enemy has done this.” They said to him, “Then do you want us to go and gather them up?”
He sent someone and had John beheaded in prison.
He called the crowd and said to them, “Listen and understand.”
Then he answered her, saying, “Woman, your faith is great! Let it happen for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
His disciples said to him, “Where will we find so much bread in this wilderness to feed such a large crowd?”
Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you collected?
When Jesus came to the [?] of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
They said, “Some say he is John the Baptist; others say he is Elijah; still others say he is Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

But so that we do not offend them, go to the sea and cast a hook. Take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take it and give it to them for me and you.
Jesus called a little child and had him stand among them.
Again, truly I tell you, if two of you agree with each other on earth about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven.
But he said to them, “Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.”

For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by other people, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let anyone who can accept this accept it.
But if we say, ‘It is from human beings,’ we are afraid of the crowd, because everyone regards John as a prophet.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Even after you saw this, you did not change your minds and believe him.
Afterward he sent his son to them, saying, “They will respect my son.”
But they paid no attention and went away, some to their fields and another to his business.
The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
One of them, an expert in the law, questioned him to test him.
But you must not let yourselves be called Rabbi, for you have one teacher, and you are all brothers.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
You say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray.
But when you see the abomination that causes desolation, spoken of through the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom his master has put in charge of his servants to give them their food at the proper time?
His master answered him, ‘You wicked and lazy servant! If you know that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter seed,
Then the elders and the chief priests of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
Peter answered him, ‘Even if they all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.’
Jesus said to him, ‘Truly I tell you, tonight, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.’
But Peter followed them at a distance, as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
For this reason, that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus killed.
They gave him wine mixed with gall to drink, but when he tasted it, he did not want to drink it.
When some of those standing there heard it, they said, ‘This man is calling for Elijah.’
And go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and look, he will go ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there.’ Look, I have told you.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had appointed for them.
